approaches.name: Semantic Search

lessons.instruction: Below you'll see three candidate documents. The next two lessons will show how keyword vs. semantic search rank them differently.

lessons.title: Keyword Search: Likely Ranking
lessons.instruction: Keyword search counts exact word overlap. See how it ranks the three documents — and notice that the most useful doc (Doc A) ends up last.

rankings.text: Best leather shoe brands for winter
Puppy chewing fixes using safe toys and redirection
How to stop dogs from biting slippers at home

lessons.insight: Keyword search rewarded surface word overlap ("shoe") and ranked the irrelevant doc highest. The most helpful answer (Doc A) landed last.

lessons.title: Same Meaning, Different Words
lessons.instruction: Pairs like these have zero shared keywords but nearly identical meaning. Semantic search captures this; keyword search cannot.
lessons.subtitle: Zero shared keywords, but almost identical meaning.
lessons.meaning_space_note: Meaning Space (simplified metaphor — not real coordinates)

lessons.title: Step 1: Embed the Query
lessons.query: How do I stop my puppy from chewing my shoes?
lessons.instruction: Notice that the query is transformed into a list of numbers (a vector). Read the explanation below and click Next when ready.
explanation: The query was turned into a list of numbers called an embedding.
These numbers encode the meaning of the sentence, not just its words.
Think of the embedding as coordinates in a "meaning space" — sentences with similar meaning land near each other.
The exact numbers do not matter for this lesson. What matters is that the model tries to place similar meanings close together.

lessons.title: Step 2: Embed Candidate Documents
lessons.instruction: Each candidate document is embedded into the same meaning space. Hover over the dots to see which document is which.

lessons.title: Step 3: Score & Rank
lessons.instruction: Each document gets a similarity score (closer in meaning = higher score). The system ranks documents by score.

rankings.title: Stop dogs from biting slippers
rankings.reason: stop ≈ prevention · dogs ≈ puppy · slippers ≈ shoes · biting ≈ chewing

rankings.title: Puppy chewing fixes with safe toys
rankings.reason: puppy = puppy · chewing = chewing · different framing

rankings.title: Best leather shoe brands for winter
rankings.reason: shoes = shoes, but the topic (shopping) is unrelated

lessons.insight: Semantic search ranks Doc A first: it captures the user's intent even though it shares no exact words with the query.

lessons.title: Recap: How Semantic Search Works
lessons.callout: Semantic search works better than keyword matching when the right answer uses different words but expresses similar meaning.
lessons.instruction: Review the three steps below. When you feel ready, click Start Quiz to test your understanding.

steps.title: Embed the query
steps.description: Turn the user's question into a numeric vector that encodes meaning.

steps.title: Embed candidate documents
steps.description: Place each candidate in the same meaning space.

steps.title: Score closeness & rank
steps.description: Rank documents by distance to the query vector. Nearer = more relevant.
